title: Certainty arises from promise plus inward sense of living faith and repentance
source_text: XXXV. Et certe qualiscunque tandem sit illa certitudo, & quocunque nomine in Christianis Scholis appelletur, in eo conveniunt omnes omnino Theologi illam non oriri solum ex divina promissione, sed etiam ex interno sensu propriae fidei & resipiscentiae, sine quo nemo recte concludere & statuere potest justitiam, vitam & salutem Verbo Dei promissam ad se pertinere, & se ejus esse, vel fore participem. Nam ut hoc aliquis legitime concludat, non sufficit ut assentiatur generalibus illis Scripturae pronunciatis, Quicunque credit in Christum remissionem habebit peccatorum in nomine ejus, Qui credit in Filium non veniet in judicium, sive damnationem, sed transivit a morte ad vitam; Sed necesse est ut vere subsumat, Atqui ego credo, id est, in me sentio & experior fidem illam quam Deus exigit, scilicet fidem vivam, quae operatur per dilectionem, & quae nunquam est sine studio bonorum operum, & serio vitae in melius mutandae proposito.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly of whatever sort that certainty finally is, and by whatever name it is called in the Christian schools, in this all theologians altogether agree that it does not arise only from the divine promise, but also from the inward sense of one’s own faith and repentance, without which no one can rightly conclude and determine that the righteousness, life, and salvation promised by the Word of God pertain to himself, and that he is or will be a partaker of it. For that someone may legitimately conclude this, it is not enough that he assent to those general pronouncements of Scripture, Whoever believes in Christ will have remission of sins in his name, Whoever believes in the Son will not come into judgment, or condemnation, but has passed from death to life; But it is necessary that he truly subsume, But I believe, that is, in myself I feel and experience that faith which God requires, namely a living faith which works through love, and which is never without the pursuit of good works and a serious purpose of amending life for the better.
pass_b_english: Assurance is not bare assent to general gospel promises.
It requires the reflective subsumption: I myself have the living, loving faith God requires.
